defect_families.evidence: No caller-controlled timestamp, cutoff, or historical-state selection is introduced; sandbox admission and launcher selection depend only on trusted runtime configuration and exact argv/path validation.
The launcher, startup selector, and shim do not perform validate-then-persist governance logic. They configure process execution and never write governed persistent state.
No durable identity is accepted from model or caller content; executable and workspace identities are derived from repository-owned paths and trusted parent declarations.

Missing or malformed authority/runtime declarations fail closed: unsupported options, missing binds, invalid roots, untrusted executable locations, or unavailable executables do not produce permissive fallback execution.
No secondary durable carrier is added. Model-visible state is confined to the isolated clone and private credential home, while publication credentials are removed.
No ordering or clock promise is introduced. Build installation, startup selection, and shim validation are deterministic over repository-owned configuration and exact runtime state.
Authorization and publication proofs are not re-aimable: the provider receives neither GitHub push credentials nor governance signing/runtime authority variables.
Unexpected bind mappings and executable locations are rejected; the shim accepts only system read-only mounts and the pinned /app/bin OpenCode mapping expected from Hunter.
This candidate uses the connector ingress with an exact authorization receipt; review and receipt evidence paths remain excluded from the substantive change set by trusted admission logic.
Connector admission authenticates the authorized connector channel rather than treating API commits as ordinary pre-push provenance; the exact receipt is bound to this branch and base.

The substantive change set is explicit and complete: Railway config, the startup selector, executable launcher, permission sandbox, and focused tests are all bound in the exact receipt and review target.
The connector authorization receipt is re-derived against every substantive blob and current main base; review/receipt artifacts remain evidence rather than implementation scope.
This pre-ready hostile review is refreshed against the exact candidate content before Ready consideration and covers the governing Issue criteria plus recurring-defect families.
No pending check is represented as success in this review. Hosted exact-head validation results are independently published by GitHub workflows.

Claims are tied to concrete code paths and focused tests: launcher installation, startup sandbox selection, strict argv parsing, credential stripping, isolated root checks, and deny-by-default permissions.
All hosted validation and review state is bound to the exact candidate head; any later content mutation makes this review stale and forces a refresh.
The runtime boundary is explicit: untrusted model execution is separated from trusted commit signing, publication, rollback, and exact-head validation.

The permission policy defaults every OpenCode capability to deny and selectively allows only project read/edit/glob/grep/LSP operations; shell, web, tasks, skills, questions, and external-directory access remain denied.

Railway’s non-privileged namespace limitation is handled without requesting privileged container capabilities. The build installs the repository-owned launcher and startup selects it explicitly, preventing a silent fallback to bubblewrap.

findings.evidence: Railway rejects bubblewrap namespace creation. The candidate replaces only that unavailable kernel isolation step with a strict fail-closed argv shim while preserving the isolated attempt clone and trusted parent publication boundary.
Provider credential exposure is blocked: GitHub push credentials, governance/runtime authority variables, HUNTER_PROMPT_* and GIT_* values are removed before OpenCode starts.
Capability escape is blocked by OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT with `* = deny` and an allowlist limited to read/edit/glob/grep/LSP, plus `--pure` and Claude-plugin disablement.

The prior P1 was real: the shim module existed but Railway never selected it. The build now installs scripts/hunter_railway_opencode_sandbox as /app/bin/hunter-railway-opencode-sandbox with mode 0755, and railway_issuer_startup.py exports that exact path as the default HUNTER_OPENCODE_SANDBOX_EXECUTABLE while preserving explicit operator overrides. Focused tests bind both installation and selection.

This application-level sandbox is intentionally weaker than an OS namespace boundary; final deployed #441 validation must confirm OpenCode honors the pinned permission contract on Railway before #437 is re-authorized.
